posts.title: How to publish a post on this blog
posts.summary: A template post showing every formatting option. Copy it, change the text, and delete it when you publish your first real post.
content: Every post on this blog lives in **posts.json**. To publish, add a new entry to the `posts` list, upload the file, and refresh the page. Nothing else needs to change.
## The fields of a post
| Field | Required | What it does |
| `slug` | yes | The post's address, e.g. `?p=my-post`. Lowercase, use dashes. |
| `title` | yes | The headline. |
| `date` | yes | `YYYY-MM-DD`. Posts are sorted newest first. |
| `summary` | no | One or two sentences shown in the list and under the title. |
| `tags` | no | Topics, used for the filter chips. |
| `cover` | no | Image URL. Without one, a generated pattern is shown. |
| `featured` | no | `true` pins the post to the large card at the top. |
| `draft` | no | `true` hides the post until you are ready. |
| `content` | yes* | The post, written in Markdown (one line per item). |
## Writing in Markdown

Use `##` for section headings and `###` for sub-sections; they also build the *On this page* menu. Wrap words in `**` for **bold** and `*` for *italics*, and write links as `[text](https://example.com)`.
### Lists
- Bullet points start with a dash
- Numbered lists start with `1.`
- Keep each item on its own line
### Quotes
> Start a line with `>` to turn it into a highlighted quote.
### Code
Fence code with three backticks and the language name to get highlighting and a copy button:
```sql
SELECT company, role, years
FROM career
ORDER BY start_year DESC;
```python
import pandas as pd
df = pd.read_csv('events.csv')
print(df.groupby('event').size())
## Before you upload
1. Check the file is valid JSON, for example with an online JSON validator.
2. Make sure every `slug` is unique.
3. Remember that quotes inside text need a backslash: `\"like this\"`.
That's it. Delete this post once your own are live.

posts.title: Welcome to my blog
posts.summary: Why I'm starting to write about analytics engineering, and what you can expect to find here.
content: After seven years of turning raw data into dashboards, metrics and warehouses, I'm starting to write down what I've learned along the way.
## What I'll write about
- **Data modeling with dbt and Snowflake**: structuring models so analysts can query them without deep technical knowledge.
- **Data quality**: dbt tests, SQL assertions and monitoring that catch problems before stakeholders do.
- **Metrics and BI**: defining KPIs teams agree on, and dashboards people actually use.
## Get in touch
If a post is useful, or you disagree with it, I'd love to hear from you on [LinkedIn](https://linkedin.com/in/meikelwis-wijaya).
